results.note: Downing Street, 20 Nov 14:36 UTC: Burnham "has today agreed a landmark package" at the Brussels summit, with "new deals on food and drink, carbon markets" (SPS deal ending export health certificates; linking the two emissions trading schemes) among "the deals agreed today"; consilium.europa.eu refuses scripted reading.

Downing Street, 20 Nov: among the deals agreed at the summit is a new Youth Experience Scheme for 18 to 31-year-olds to live, work, study and travel for up to three years, capped and visa-based, i.e. agreed with its main terms (age range, length of stay).
Senate roll call 269, 19 Nov: H.Con.Res. 93 rejected 48-51, one Yea short of the 49 threshold (three Republicans for, Fetterman against, Murphy absent per AP via ADN).
Senate roll call 269, 19 Nov: the concurrent resolution H.Con.Res. 93 was rejected 48-51.

Carbon Brief: after the second draft of 19 Nov, the third draft cover decision "initially expected on Friday afternoon" was published only at 3am local time on Sunday 22 Nov; its live blog of 21 Nov 17:29 UTC confirms no new draft had come more than 24 hours after the scheduled close.
No new version of the cover decision was published on 20 Nov (Antalya time): the third draft came at 3am on 22 Nov, and it too has no direct reference to the transition away from fossil fuels.
N1/FoNet, 19 Nov: Aleksandar Čupić (Student List) was elected speaker of the National Assembly with 140 votes against 97 for SNS's Stojan Radenović, above the 126 required.
Senate roll call 270, 19 Nov: H.R. 2347, as amended, passed 62-33 (after cloture 65-31, roll call 268).
ONS first estimate, 20 Nov: retail sales volumes rose by 0.7% in October 2026 (after a fall of 0.6% in September, revised from 0.4%).
Cenový věstník 128/2026 of 20 Nov sets the maximum diesel price for 21-23 Nov 2026 at 44.53 CZK per litre including VAT (petrol 39.47).
Statistics Bureau release note of 20 Nov: national CPI for October 2026 (2025=100), all items 103.1, up 2.3% year on year (ex fresh food 2.2%, ex fresh food and energy 2.2%).
